Midjourney V7 Just Dropped — And It's the Update We've Been Waiting For

After months of speculation, Midjourney V7 is finally here. As someone who's used every version since V1, here's my honest take on what changed.

Finally

Midjourney V7 dropped this week, and I've been testing it non-stop for 48 hours. I've been using Midjourney since version 1 — back when it could barely generate coherent human faces. We've come a long way.

Here's what you need to know.

What's New

Consistency is dramatically improved. The single biggest improvement. I generated a character in one prompt, then used that character in 10 different scenarios. The consistency was shockingly good. This alone makes V7 worth the upgrade.

Text rendering actually works now. Remember when Midjourney couldn't render text to save its life? V7 can actually render readable text in images. It's not perfect, but it's usable.

Better understanding of complex prompts. I threw some ridiculously complex descriptions at it — multi-character scenes, specific lighting conditions, unusual compositions. V7 handled them significantly better than V6.

What's Still Missing

Video generation. Competitors are adding video. Midjourney remains image-only. For how long?

Real-time generation. It's still slow. When you need 50 variations quickly, you're waiting.

The Verdict

If you're a Midjourney user, V7 is a mandatory upgrade. The consistency alone changes everything. I can finally use Midjourney for real client work where characters need to appear across multiple images.

If you're not using Midjourney yet and need image generation, V7 is the best entry point yet.

Rating: 8.5/10 — The update we've been waiting for. Finally ready for professional work.
